item.title: RBI to conduct 4-day Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction under LAF on November 09, 2026
item.description:

item.title: Auction of 91-Day, 182-Day and 364-Day Treasury Bills
item.description:
Reserve Bank of India announces the auction of Government of India Treasury Bills as per the following details:

Sr. No. Treasury Bill Notified Amount
(₹ crore)		 Auction Date Settlement Date
1 91-Day 8,000 November 11, 2026
(Wednesday)		 November 12, 2026
(Thursday)
2 182-Day 8,000
3 364-Day 7,000
  Total 23,000    

The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions specified in the General Notification F.No.4(2)-B(W&M)/2018 dated March 26, 2025, issued by Government of India, as amended from time to time. State Governments, Union Territories with legislature, eligible Provident Funds in India, designated Foreign Central Banks and any person or institution specified by the Bank in this regard can participate on non-competitive basis, the allocation for which will be outside the notified amount. Individuals can also participate on non-competitive basis, as retail investors. For retail investors, the allocation will be restricted to a maximum of 5 percent of the notified amount. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).

The auction will be Price based using multiple price method. Bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India’s Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber system) on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, during the below given timings:

Category of Bids Timing
Competitive 10:30 am - 11:30 am
Non-Competitive 10:30 am - 11:00 am

Results will be announced on the day of the auction.

Payment by successful bidders will have to be made on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190), before the auction timing ends, in the prescribed form. The form can be downloaded from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx). In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted at email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).

Ajit Prasad           
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)

item.title: Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian Direct Investment Entities for 2025-26
item.description:
Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-261 round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment. The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports. The variations in outstanding foreign assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements.

Key highlights:

  • Of the total number of Indian entities reporting foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or overseas direct investment (ODI), around 97 per cent entities were unlisted as at end-March 2026, and also held a major share in total FDI equity capital (at face value) in India (Tables 1 and 2A).

  • Non-financial companies accounted for more than 90 per cent of the FDI equity at face value (Table 2B).

  • In terms of market value, listed and unlisted companies had almost equal share in total FDI equity capital as at end-March 2026, however, 96.6 per cent of the FDI debt is held by unlisted companies (Table 3A).

  • In rupee terms, the ratio of inward FDI to ODI moderated to 4.2 times as on end-March 2026 from 5.5 times a year ago (Table 3B).

  • Other investment liabilities [viz., trade credit, loans, currency and deposits, and other payables with unrelated (third party) non-resident entities] recorded a growth of 11.9 per cent (y-o-y) in rupee terms as on end-March 2026; other investment assets with unrelated non-residents also rose by 16.1 per cent during the same period (Table 4).

  • The United States of America (16.5 per cent) followed by Mauritius (14.5 per cent), Singapore (13.7 per cent) and the United Kingdom (10.8 per cent) were the top sources of outstanding FDI. In case of ODI, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America were the top destinations together accounting for more than 50 per cent share (Tables 5 and 6).

  • Manufacturing sector accounted for the highest share in the total outstanding FDI equity capital at market value (50.1 per cent), while 45 per cent share was held by services sector (Tables 7 and 8).

(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager

Press Release: 2026-2027/1463

item.title: Sectoral Deployment of Credit by NBFC – September 2026
item.description:
Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) for the month of September 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement1.

On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs’ credit registered a growth of 15.4 per cent in September 2026 as compared to 13.3 per cent a year ago.

Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended September 30, 2026, are given below:

  • Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.8 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as against 5.2 per cent a year ago.

  • Credit growth in industry sector declined to 7.4 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as compared with 10.2 per cent in September 2025. Within industry, credit growth in ‘infrastructure’ remained subdued.

  • Credit growth in services sector moderated to 17.3 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 from 23.0 per cent a year ago. While credit to ‘commercial real estate’ marked buoyant expansion, ‘trade’ and ‘transport operators’ segments also witnessed higher credit growth.

  • Retail loans growth accelerated to 21.9 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 compared to 16.8 per cent a year ago. Within retail sector, ‘housing loans’, ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘vehicle loans’ witnessed accelerated credit growth.

Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    

Press Release: 2026-2027/1461

1 Provisional data as reported on the last day of the month. Sectoral credit data of NBFCs are based on sample of (i) NBFCs in Upper and Middle Layers, and (ii) HFCs, accounting for about 87 per cent of total credit with respect to data published in ‘Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25’ (RTP 2024-25, outstanding as on September 2025).

item.title: Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha, Bengaluru - Extension of Period
item.description:
The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha, Bengaluru vide Directive No. DoS.CO.UCB.BSD-III.D-2/12.23.283/2019-20 dated January 02, 2020, for a period of six months up to close of business on July 10, 2020. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on November 10, 2026.

2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of powers vested in it under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of six months from close of business on November 10, 2026 to close of business on May 10, 2027, subject to review.

3. The aforesaid extension and /or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should not per-se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the financial position of the bank.

4. Other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference, shall remain unchanged.

(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
